messages.subject: different output between Rstan and Stan running from the command line
parts:

yajuan$ ./gpandbbpred-0421-1 --data=sim.0426-2.csv --chain.id=1
STAN SAMPLING COMMAND

init = random initialization
init tries = 1
samples = samples.csv
append_samples = 0
save_warmup = 0
seed = 1327658651 (randomly generated)
chain_id = 1 (default)
iter = 2000
warmup = 1000
thin = 1
equal_step_sizes = 0
nondiag_mass = 0
leapfrog_steps = -1
max_treedepth = 10
epsilon = -1
epsilon_pm = 0
delta = 0.5
gamma = 0.05
Iteration:   1 / 1000 [  0%]  (Warmup)
Iteration:  10 / 1000 [  1%]  (Warmup)
Iteration:  20 / 1000 [  2%]  (Warmup)
Iteration:  30 / 1000 [  3%]  (Warmup)
Iteration:  40 / 1000 [  4%]  (Warmup)
Iteration:  50 / 1000 [  5%]  (Warmup)

However, in Rstan,

sim.data<-read_rdump("stan-file/sim.0426-2.csv")
gp_sim <- stan(file="gpandbbpred-0421-1.stan", data=sim.data,
+ iter=500, chains=3);

TRANSLATING MODEL 'gpandbbpred-0421-1' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

Warning: integer division implicitly rounds to integer. Found int division: get_base1(vec_n,j,"vec_n",1) / N
 Positive values rounded down, negative values rounded up or down in platform-dependent way.

error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

Thanks for the report. Jiqiang -- can you take a look
at why RStan is stopping here? Maybe Yajuan can send
you her model and data so you can replicate it. Or maybe
a simple test case is enough. I'm wondering where the
non-positive def matrix came from (data, transformed data,
or transformed parameters).

Yajuan: this diagnostic you need to pay attention to:

> Warning: integer division implicitly rounds to integer. Found int division: get_base1(vec_n,j,"vec_n",1) / N
> Positive values rounded down, negative values rounded up or down in platform-dependent way.

You had "vec_n[j] / N" somewhere and both vec_n[j] and N are
integers. Integer arithmetic rounds, e.g., 1/3 = 0, 7/2 = 3, etc.
which is probably not what you want.

More below.

> Iteration: 40 / 1000 [ 4%] (Warmup)

Can you try it with the same seed? You should see that same warning message
in the command line version.

> However, in Rstan,
>
> sim.data<-read_rdump("stan-file/sim.0426-2.csv")
> gp_sim <- stan(file="gpandbbpred-0421-1.stan", data=sim.data,
> + iter=500, chains=3);

>
> Warning: integer division implicitly rounds to integer. Found int division: get_base1(vec_n,j,"vec_n",1) / N
> Positive values rounded down, negative values rounded up or down in platform-dependent way.
>
> COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'gpandbbpred-0421-1' NOW.
> SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'gpandbbpred-0421-1' NOW (CHAIN 1).
> Error : Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_log(d): Covariance matrix is not positive definite. Covariance
> matrix(0,0) is 1.4411103071065978.
> error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

But the R version shouldn't crap out here. If a matrix isn't
positive definite, the sample should get rejected.

Looks like there still needs to be a catch somewhere.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] different output between Rstan and Stan running from the command line
parts:
Thanks for reporting the problem.

It is a bug in RStan: during initializing the parameters, RStan does not try/catch exceptions as in Stan (here the exception is not  thrown during samling).  I have fixed this bug and pushed the code. 

By the way, I think the error message in Stan (an example shown for this model) for this case is not ideal as it says about "...Metropolis rejected ...."  But here we are in the process of initializing parameters. 


$ ./gpandbbpred-0421-1 --data=sim.0426-2.csv --iter=10

Informational Message: The parameter state is about to be Metropolis rejected due to the following underlying, non-fatal (really) issue (and please ignore that what comes next might say 'error'): Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_log(d): Covariance matrix is not positive definite. Covariance matrix(0,0) is 5.3603975246673192.
If the problem persists across multiple draws, you might have a problem with an initial state or a gradient somewhere.
 If the problem does not persist, the resulting samples will still be drawn from the posterior.

STAN SAMPLING COMMAND
data = sim.0426-2.csv
init = random initialization
init tries = 2

samples = samples.csv
append_samples = 0
save_warmup = 0

seed = 1353173246 (randomly generated)
......
gamma = 0.05

Iteration: 1 / 10 [ 10%]  (Adapting)
.....
Iteration: 10 / 10 [100%]  (Sampling)

Elapsed Time: 0.01 seconds

--
Jiqiang

Thanks for reporting the problem.

It is a bug in RStan: during initializing the parameters, RStan does not try/catch exceptions as in Stan (here the exception is not  thrown during samling).  I have fixed this bug and pushed the code. 

By the way, I think the error message in Stan (an example shown for this model) for this case is not ideal as it says about "...Metropolis rejected ...."  But here we are in the process of initializing parameters.
